about: The Carnet « Le sommaire » contract (plan piste 9, briefs/plan-carnet-sommaire.md; prose in sommaire.md): what the bridge answers the phones for the new Carnet, the same file for the bridge and both apps. `types`: each answer's shape in a small type language (string, int, number, bool, any; `T?` nullable; `[T]` a list; `map:T` an object of any keys; `enum:a|b` one of; a capitalised name: another type; in an object, `key?` an optional key). `routes`: each route, the brick that brings it (S1…S6), its answer's type and an example answer from the demo Carnet (`fake-bridge/`, made by bridge-rs src/notebook/categories.rs `write_fake_bridge`, BIPAGENTS_WRITE_FAKE_BRIDGE=1). `additive`: the keys the sommaire adds to the routes the installed 1.0 apps read — nothing else changes there (bridge/tests_blackbox/test_carnet_sommaire.py compares every such answer with the 1.0 bridge's, these keys taken out). Checked by bridge-rs `the_sommaire_contract_holds_together` (every example has its type, every type is defined).

titles_proposed._note: Names for the screens (S4 serves them, `title` in the answers); the apps never show an id. Alex, 22/11: « Personnes » (not « Gens »), the other French names stand for now; en/de/es/nl follow (People, Personen, Personas, Personen), to be read by a speaker.

additive_elsewhere._note: keys S3 adds to routes of the 1.0 apps outside the Carnet (ignored by them as the others)

ids: Item ids are stable and never hold a text, a path or a file's name: `page:<page key>` (its frontmatter `id`, else `f` + 10 hex of its path's hash), `line:<page key>:<10 hex of the line folded>` (`:2`, `:3`… for the same line said again on the page), `task:<id>`, `record:<id>`, `doc:<agent>:<12 hex of the file's name>`. A line's `page` is its page's Item id: its title and `aliases` apply to the line (« aniv marc »).
dates: The index never depends on the day it is made, so its version and ETag change only with the Carnet: its categories never hold `dates`; an item carries `date` (a day, YYYY-MM-DD) or `yearly` (« MM-DD »: a birthday, an anniversary). The phone adds `dates` itself: `yearly` always, a `date` from `dated.before` days ago to `dated.after` days ahead (90, 730). A date without a year that says nothing yearly is the day nearest to when it was noted (« devis reçu le 3 octobre »), never every year; « 1/2 » is not a date (« 14/11 » is). A record is dated by its next date only (a warranty's end, a renewal, an end, an expiry, a booking's day), never a purchase's day. The bridge's other answers (search, summary, a category's page, today's routes) give `dates` as of the bridge's day.
counts: A note with two categories counts in each (a category's `count`, a search's `counts.<id>`: the chips filter on any of them); `total` and `counts.all` count each note once; a search lists a note once, in the group of its first category.
index: GET /v1/notebook/index. **Tables**: `stop`, `neighbours` and `dates` are the Carnet's language's, and the app's (`?lang=`) when it differs (bridge-rs notebook/search_words.rs; the fake bridge keeps its drafts); each language's stop words (its words of the lexicon's and of a spoken question). **Left out**: a page whose path, a document whose file's name holds a reference (with its lines; the phone opens a page by its path); an agent's web page whose title does; a real file's extension is no part of a reference; a reference in a title, an « En bref », a section's title, a task's title or a document's name is masked (« … »); a document's text without its lines holding a number or a reference (read on the raw line) and without words of digits but a year or one or two digits; two files of the same name: one item, the newest. **Epoch**: a word the bridge draws when its Carnet's history starts again (made, restored from a backup, moved to another place, reinstalled); the ETag is `"<epoch>-v<version>-<languages of the tables>"` (opaque to the phones); a `since` of another epoch, greater than the version, or that the bridge no longer has, gives everything (`full: true`). **Diff** (`full: false`): `items` are the notes added or changed (whole), `removed` the ids gone; the tables (`stop`, `neighbours`, `dates`, `dated`, `limits`, `kept`) are whole in every answer, full or diff, never left out; `kept` (S4) is every space's kept searches (`KeptShort`, a key at its default left out), and a change of theirs is a version of its own (`items` and `removed` empty). **Size**: `limits.bytes` counts the compact JSON as sent (no spaces, before compression); an item leaves out every key at its default (null, false, an empty text or list, `part: main`, `space: perso`; only `id`, `kind` and `open` are always there: an absent `title`, `line` or `fold` is empty, absent `categories` none), about 6 MB for 20 000 lines, so the line limit cuts first; the answer is gzip-compressed (`Content-Encoding: gzip`) when the request accepts it. The bridge alone keeps the copy within the limits (the phone never trims): over a limit, out first: archived lines, the oldest noted first; then archived pages; then the other lines, the oldest noted first; `truncated: true`, `online_only` the bar's text. Every Carnet answer carries `Cache-Control: no-store` (the index, the search, the offline copy of today, every /v1/notebook route and the family's): no HTTP cache keeps it.
summary: GET /v1/notebook/summary, /category/{id}, /kept, POST /searched (S4, bridge-rs notebook/summary.rs). **Counted on the phone's copy** (`Index` items, the search's rule): a category's `count` is its notes, `dates` as of the bridge's day; `total` each note once; Santé is never in the copy. **Lines**: in `categories.order.personal`; one with no note is left out; `health` always last (not in `pro`): `count: null`, `hint: ""`, `locked: true`, no `first`. **`hint`**: the category's 3 latest searches made (`searched`), else its 3 latest distinct titles (a line's title is its page's), joined by « , ». **`first`**: in `people`, « Toi » (the person's own page); else the category's latest note. **Latest** (`first`, `recent`, the titles of `hint`): the newest `noted` first (a page has none: after, in the copy's order); in `dates` and its sub-filters, what is still to come first (the soonest first), then the past (the latest first). **`card`**: the first that waits of `sorted` (S2's card), `ask` and `follow` (the question of the day and a follow-up still open today: their conversation cards), `misplaced`, `review` (the week's); each as its own route shows it, answered by its own route; null in `pro`. **`spaces`** (S5): the setting « Séparer Perso, Pro et Famille » off, `[]` (the app keeps its own « Moi | Famille »); on, `perso` (« Perso »), then `pro` (« Pro ») when the person has a Pro agent or a Pro note, `selected` the space asked (`all`: none); the app adds its Famille (the household's rule, in the app until S6) and shows the selector with two choices or more, asking `perso` or `pro`. **`version`**: the copy's (`Index.version`). **Sub-filters** (`categories.filters`, their `count` among the category's notes; `filter` narrows `recent`): `invoices` a note (not a record) whose title or line has a word starting with factur, factuur, invoice, rechnung; `contracts` a contract record, or such a note with contrat, contract, vertrag, contrato; `warranties` a purchase record (in Papiers: it has a warranty), or garanti, warrant, guarant, gewahrleist; `to_pay` an open task, a subscription whose renewal is to come, another note (not a record) whose day is to come; `subscriptions` a subscription record, or abonn, subscri, suscrip, the word abo(s); `purchases` a purchase record, or achat, achet, purchase, bought, gekauft, compra, aankoop, gekocht; `this_week` a day from today to Sunday, `this_month` to the month's last day, `later` after it; `close` « Toi », a page marked « proche » and their lines, `others` the rest. **Kept searches** (`state.json` `kept_searches`): the words as typed (a date phrase too, its interval taken again each day), a title, 6 a space (`all`, `perso`, `pro`), a category when kept from its page; `count` = `counts.all` of the sommaire's search of those words (in that category and space); never a number or a reference, never Santé; in the copy as `KeptShort` (every space's), whole in each answer, the copy's version moving with them. **Searches made** (`searched.json` beside the state: never in a page, the state, the copy, an agent's tool): 3 a category and a space, the newest first, the same words once; without a category, under the category of the search's best result; never Santé, a number or a reference, a single letter; `at` in UTC. **« Oublie ça »** takes the kept searches (every space: the copy moves to a new version) and the searches made whose words, or a kept one's title, say what is forgotten (folded, whole words; a person's first name too when their page is forgotten whole). **Spaces (S5, bridge-rs notebook/spaces.rs)**: a note's space is its page's (`space: pro` in its header, by a Pro agent's new page with the setting on, by the person's « Ranger dans… », or by hand in Obsidian) or the person's mark (a record, a task, a document, a single line); `perso` is what is not Pro, `all` everything. Santé is in no space: its line shows in `all` and `perso` (locked), never in `pro`; its page (`category/health?private=1`) and its search ignore `space`. **Kept searches by view**: `all` lists every space's (the setting off: everything together), `perso` Perso's and those kept in `all` (the setting on: those of before are in Perso), `pro` Pro's; each `Kept.space` is its own (null for `all`); 6 a view when kept (a view may show more after the setting changed: nothing is dropped); its `count` in the view's space. **Searches made**: each space its own (`all`, `perso`, `pro`), never mixed. **`version` and `epoch`**: the copy's; a version is compared only with its epoch (the bridge started again: another epoch, versions from 1). **A copy cut** (`truncated`): the counts are the copy's as sent, archives included. **Santé open**: a search made in Santé, or with `private=1`, is sent with `category: health` or `private: true`, or not at all: never kept. **Dropping searches made**: `DELETE /v1/notebook/searched` (one, by its words, or all; a space, a category): the person's gesture for a search whose words are nowhere in the Carnet, that « Oublie ça » cannot find. **The moment's card** never speaks of health: no point of Santé in `misplaced` (whatever its words), no `ask` or `follow` whose question, choices or task touch health. **« Oublie ça » and a person's name**: their name word only (the first of 3 letters or more that is no stop word: « La nounou » → « nounou », never « la »).
feasts: `dates.feasts` are rules, never days, so the copy does not change with the day: a fixed day (`month`, `day`: Christmas) or days from Easter (`easter`: Ascension 39); `dates.easter` gives Easter's day for this year and the nine after. A feast's day is its next one from the phone's day (« avant Noël » on 26 December: the coming one); a phrase whose interval would end before it starts is ignored.
records: Never a number or a reference in the index: a record's `line` leaves out its number, its booking reference and its source, and any value that holds a reference (bridge-rs categories.rs `holds_reference`: offline.rs `numbered` — an ID number, a word of 6 characters or more with 3 digits or more — and a code of letters and digits such as « HR-55821 », never a price, a date or a time); a page's line that holds one is not in the index at all, nor a line linking an archived mail (`[[archive:…]]`), as in the offline copy of today. The health part is never there; the shared Carnet's lines that look like health are (decision 6).
spaces: A note's `space` is `perso` or `pro`; a request asks `all`, `perso` or `pro` (S5). A page's: `space: pro` in its frontmatter (Perso: none; `Pro` in any case read as pro, another value as Perso); its lines, its tasks (their first [[link]]) and the documents linked to it or named on it have its space unless the person filed one elsewhere (`state.json` `space_marks`, keys only); a record is Perso unless filed in Pro. The setting « Séparer Perso, Pro et Famille » (`separate_spaces`, off at first) decides only where a Pro agent makes its new pages (Pro when on) and the sommaire's selector; the filter `?space=` reads the notes' space whatever the setting. Titles (the home's groups of agents): fr Perso / Pro, en Personal / Work, de Privat / Arbeit, es Personal / Trabajo, nl Privé / Werk (proposed).
page_text: The page's own text (`text` in GET /v1/notebook/page, the file on disk) gains `categories:` (1 or 2 ids, a YAML list), `categories_by:` and, with S5, `space: pro` in its frontmatter; the 1.0 apps never read them (the comparison takes them out of `text` too).
